claim: Repository contains 73 canonical channels, 2149 videos, 2137 real transcripts, 12 placeholders, 38 standard packages, 44 channels with video-level data.
notes: Verified via direct SQL query against channels/videos/transcripts tables 2026-09-25.

claim: Exactly 6 of the 73 channels are Senior Health (direct/near-direct): Dr. Ares Senior, Senior Health Hub, Doctor Thomas, Dr. Okoro, Dr. Elias Senior Health, Dr. Aliza Wright | Advice. No adjacent/hidden Senior Health channels exist among the other 67.
notes: Verified via channel-name review AND keyword scan of all 2149 video titles for 25+ health/aging terms; non-health channels showed only incidental noise-matches (e.g. 'fall' in unrelated contexts).

claim: All 6 Senior Health channels have usable video-level data (STANDARD_PACKAGE or HISTORICAL_FORMAT, real transcripts). No internal data-completeness gap in this cohort.
notes: 306 total videos across the 6 channels; 305 real transcripts, 1 placeholder (Doctor Thomas).

claim: None of the 6 Senior Health channels has forensic video/visual editing evidence (all NOT_AVAILABLE); this matches the project-wide state where only CH-000004 (not in this cohort) has forensic video evidence.
notes: Editing/Visual Intelligence is NOT_AVAILABLE for this cohort; thumbnail analysis limited to title-text and thumbnail_url presence, not pixel-level forensics.

claim: Topic clusters 'Digestion/Gut' (median 1.75x, 46% outlier rate, n=26) and 'Mobility/Falls/Balance' (median 1.67x, 40% outlier rate, n=20) are the two strongest-performing internal topic clusters; Cancer (median 0.54x) and Kidney/Skin/Nails signs (0.59x) are the weakest.
notes: Topic tagging is keyword-regex based (12 categories), not human-verified per video; directional not exact.

claim: The title 'One SIMPLE Change to How You Walk That Could Save Your Life After 70' (or near-identical variant) was published on Doctor Thomas (2026-06-19, 1,004,391 views) and Dr. Aliza Wright | Advice (2026-06-26, 219,009 views) 7 days apart. Different video_ids and durations, so not literal duplicates, but same script/topic template.
notes: Per AGENTS.md rule 9, treated as ONE topic-level demand signal, not two independent breakout observations, in all downstream synthesis.

claim: Matched pair (Dr. Okoro, Kidney/Bladder topic): 'Your Kidneys Are Begging You to Eat These 5 Vegetables' scored 56.9x channel median; near-identical title 'Your Kidneys Are Begging You to Eat These 6 Foods If You Have Diabetes' scored 0.23x. Same channel, same title template, 247x performance gap.
notes: Direct counter-evidence against any 'title template alone predicts success' rule.

claim: Google Trends search term 'clove water' (US, past 12 months) rose from ~40 (Sep 2025) to peak ~100 (late Feb 2026), then declined to a ~50-65 plateau through mid-2026. Senior Health Hub's single largest breakout (3,088,021 views, 'Put 1 Clove in Coffee...', 2026-04-28) was published roughly 2 months AFTER the trend peak, when search interest had already declined ~35-45%.
notes: Trend timing does not explain the single biggest breakout; trend rise may explain the channel's decision to enter/expand the cluster in the first place (Sep 2025 onward), but not why this specific video outperformed ~40 sibling videos on the same ingredient.

claim: Google Trends search term 'balance exercises for seniors' (US, past 12 months) shows stable evergreen interest (~50-90 range) with no discernible seasonal spike across the full window.
notes: Supports EVERGREEN-DEMAND classification for the Mobility pillar, corroborating the internal cross-channel breakout pattern (EV-006).

claim: Google Trends search term 'diabetic foot signs' (US, past 12 months) shows sparse, near-zero baseline with occasional small spikes - low and noisy search volume, not a robust evergreen search term at the national level.
notes: Weakens SEARCH-LIKELY explanation for Dr. Okoro's 2484x outlier; strengthens POSSIBLE-RECOMMENDATION-EXPANSION hypothesis.

claim: YouTube search for 'diabetic foot signs after 60' surfaced at least 2 unrelated small channels ('بوابة الصحة بالعربي' - 36 views, 'Health Insight' - 20 views) publishing near-verbatim titles/scripts to Dr. Okoro's mega-breakout ('Cardiologist Warns: 9 Foot Signs of Hidden Diabetes After 60', 494,473 views). Both external copies badly underperformed despite using the same topic/title template.
notes: Strong evidence the topic+script is being farmed across multiple faceless channels (a content-mill pattern); only one execution broke out, suggesting packaging/channel-authority/algorithm-luck rather than topic demand alone drove the outcome.

claim: A YouTube search for 'clove water elderly benefits' surfaced multiple unrelated external creators with videos well outside the 73-channel repository earning 1M-5.9M+ views on the same core topic (e.g. Dr. Eric Berg DC - 5.9M views; a 'parasitic worms' angle - 2.6M views), confirming clove water is a pre-existing, large, cross-market wellness genre, not a niche invented by our internal channel.
notes: External validation for the Digestive Health pillar's demand claim.

claim: video_type field is inconsistent across the corpus (None/regular video/video/Short/shorts - 5 distinct values across 2149 videos, 159 with no value at all). Not resolved; per AGENTS.md Phase 94 rule, treated as UNKNOWN where unresolved rather than fabricated.
notes: Data-quality caveat carried into the master video table and all downstream analysis.

claim: No first-party YouTube Analytics exist for any competitor or for our future channel. CTR, impressions, retention, AVD, watch time, and traffic-source data are unavailable for all conclusions in this report.
notes: All discovery-mode labels (SEARCH-LIKELY/BROWSE-LIKELY/etc.) in this report are hypotheses, not proven causation.
